clue.text: Rubber glove plant?

blocks.note: first meaning: a well-known British brand of yellow household rubber gloves
second meaning: a garden flower with orange or yellow blooms

explanation.walkthrough: Marigold is the brand name British shoppers use for washing-up gloves, so the two words read like one odd item but are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a trademarked brand of kitchen gloves and a common bright-flowered garden annual.

clue.text: Son's left diving equipment somewhere in the Caribbean

indicators.note: left here means departed, so that letter goes away from the word

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
the breathing apparatus divers wear underwater

explanation.surface: A boy has walked off with his snorkelling gear while on a Caribbean holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son's left' reads as 'the son has left', so S departs from SCUBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is an island nation lying in the Caribbean Sea, so it is a place in that region.

clue.text: Work in arts is random

indicators.note: random means in no set order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble that creative work in the arts is haphazard.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain is to exert yourself hard, a synonym for labour or effort as a verb.

clue.text: Scent victory at last in real struggle

indicators.note: a struggle is a tussle, so these letters get thrown about into a new order
in tells us the preceding letters are placed inside the following ones

blocks.note: at last means in the end, giving the word end

explanation.surface: A fragrance marks a hard-won triumph after a genuine fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' gives a whole word meaning 'finally', not just a final letter, which is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant shrub whose oil is a classic perfume, so it names a smell or scent.

clue.text: Book cover gives dirt on Calvin Klein in, yes, German and French

indicators.note: in places the designer's initials within the German word that follows

blocks.note: the fashion designer's initials, used as his brand

explanation.surface: A paperback jacket promising gossip about the designer Calvin Klein, written in two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here means placed before, in a down clue; the designer's initials sit inside the German word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust jacket is the removable paper wrapper protecting a hardback, i.e. its outer cover.

clue.text: Free soldiers at the right moment!

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers are RE, and the setter reads soldiers as RE's, the Royal Engineers'
a cue is the signal telling you the right moment to act

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to liberate the troops just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; the setter treats the soldiers' cue as RE'S CUE, an S the clue never prints.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to free them from danger or captivity, so the verb free is a synonym.

clue.text: Small container, say, for bread?

indicators.note: say signals that we go by how the word is spoken rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a bag with the diminutive -ette would be a little bag

explanation.surface: Asking whether a little box or pouch would do for carrying a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the answer sounds like a bag plus the -ette ending that means small, as in kitchenette.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is the long thin French loaf, so it is a kind of bread.

clue.text: English 10p, one with Queen reversed, is to become invalid

indicators.note: reversed tells us to read the royal abbreviation backwards

blocks.note: X is ten in Roman numerals
I is one in Roman numerals
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: An old English ten-pence coin bearing the Queen's head is no longer legal tender.
explanation.walkthrough: 10p is split into X and P. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport or licence that expires runs out and stops being valid, so expire means to become invalid.

clue.text: Charm consisting of a cross on a letter

blocks.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
a letter, here T, placed after the rest

explanation.surface: A lucky charm made of a cross on a letter, like a pendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a religious symbol but means a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is an object worn as a protective trinket against harm, which is a charm.

clue.text: Satnav is an essential for travel to certain countries

definitions.text: essential for travel to certain countries

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of satnav, all of is and the start of an

explanation.surface: A claim that a satellite navigation device is indispensable for travelling abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no signal word: the answer sits in plain sight inside the opening words, which also lend 'an' to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is the official entry permit some countries require before visitors may enter.

clue.text: Novice tore into a very quiet Italian church

indicators.note: into tells us the first piece is put inside what follows

blocks.note: pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
rent is the past tense of rend, to tear

explanation.surface: A beginner charged into a hushed church in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tore' looks like a verb of rushing, but it is the past tense of rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is a learner of a trade, a newcomer still being taught, which is a novice.

clue.text: Relative's money is keeping Uncle Sam

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one word contains the other

blocks.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States

explanation.surface: A family member's cash is propping up the American government.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the relative is the money holding Uncle Sam.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is the child of an aunt or uncle, a family member and so a relative.

clue.text: Still try it on as a cook

indicators.note: to cook the books is to fiddle them, so these letters are tampered with

explanation.surface: Advice to someone working in a kitchen to have a go at being a chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationary means not moving, the adjectival sense of still.

clue.text: Embarrassed about theologian putting in appearance

indicators.note: putting in tells us one piece is inserted inside another

explanation.surface: Someone abashed about a scholar of religion turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: DD (Doctor of Divinity) is the usual crossword theologian; 'appearance' means looks, not turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-faced describes blushing with shame, the visible sign of being embarrassed.

clue.text: Famine makes daughter heart-broken

indicators.note: something broken is smashed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mother's grief that hunger leaves her daughter heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart-broken' is one word in the surface but splits into the fodder and its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity, and a famine is a severe scarcity of food.

clue.text: Old Poet Laureate crafts sonnet about new young leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, so we keep the opening letter of each word
to craft is to fashion something, so these letters are worked into a new form
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the others

blocks.note: the first letters of new and young

explanation.surface: A former laureate writes a sonnet about fresh young figures in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' here applies to the two words before it, taking their opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson held the post of Britain's Poet Laureate in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Out of money with number not working

explanation.surface: Penniless, and the phone number has been cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is broken is out of order, so it is not functioning.

clue.text: Author's not written about sad lives

indicators.note: written about means written around, so one word is set around the other
sad suggests something in a sorry state, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A writer has never chronicled unhappy lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist writes fiction books, so is a kind of author.

clue.text: Clever commercial's first-rate: love it!

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word joined to it

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A viewer raves that a clever TV advert is top-notch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First-rate' looks like praise but splits into the signal 'first' and the word rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and quick-witted, a synonym for clever.

clue.text: Appointed as design engineers

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or construct, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone has been hired as a design engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineers' looks like a plural noun but is a verb working on design.
explanation.definitionFit: To be assigned to a post is to be allotted or named to it, i.e. appointed.

clue.text: Caught in lady setter's stratagem

indicators.note: in tells us the first letter is placed inside the rest

blocks.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A puzzle compiler's cunning plan is trapped by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside SHE ME, after the S. Calling the setter 'me' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a crafty plan or plot, the same as a stratagem.

clue.text: From time to time I have reason to act

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: Someone admits they only occasionally feel driven to do anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From time to time' looks like one phrase meaning occasionally; here each time is clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the cause that drives someone to do something, their reason for acting.

clue.text: Mentioned house in the country style

indicators.note: mentioned means said out loud, so we go by sound

blocks.note: a manor is a country house

explanation.surface: A country house was described in a particular fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A manner is a way of doing something, so it means style or mode.

clue.text: Slum riot hasn't yet lost heart, having won changes

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter drops out
a riot is wild disorder, so these letters are scrambled
changes means alters, a second signal to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: A shanty district's unrest hasn't died down, having won concessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' backs up the riot signal; the surface reads 'Slum riot' as one news item.
explanation.definitionFit: A shantytown is a settlement of makeshift shacks on a city's edge, a poor area or slum.

clue.text: Rippling lake's variety of greens

indicators.note: rippling water is disturbed, so these letters are stirred about

explanation.surface: The rippling lake shows many shades of green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' here means leafy vegetables, not colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Kale is a leafy cabbage, one kind of the green vegetables known as greens.

clue.text: Sleeps with some of the fishes?

blocks.note: first meaning: kip is British slang for sleep
second meaning: a kip is the hooked lower jaw of a male salmon, part of a fish

explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the gangster phrase 'sleeps with the fishes', meaning lies dead at the bottom of the sea. Kip is also a rarer word for the hooked jaw of a spawning salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: Kips is slang for naps, and also the plural of a term for part of a salmon's anatomy.

clue.text: Oriental doctor has nothing after over year developing organism

indicators.note: over suggests turning something over, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: An Eastern physician is left with nothing after more than a year of growing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like 'more than' but signals turning the year round; MB is a medical degree, a stock crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is an organism in its earliest stage of growth, before birth or hatching.

clue.text: Spring lock outside and enter without permission

indicators.note: outside means one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A burglar springs a lock from outside to break in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' and 'lock' look like burglary terms, but are water and hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to go onto someone's land or property without the right to, i.e. intrude.
